add_source.description:
Register WHERE knowledge comes from (a document, web page, chat or note) and get a source_id.
            Pass that source_id to assert_fact for every fact you take from it: the fact then points back at the
            source, why() can show it, and forget_source / quarantine_source can remove or isolate everything
            that came from it. Safe to repeat: the same uri returns the same source_id.

uri.description: Where it lives (URL or path). The same uri always gives the same source id. Omit for a pasted note: an id is derived from the title and text.

anchor_fact.description:

        fact becomes SUSPECT and shows up in facts_to_verify. Facts derived from a Source whose uri is a file path
        are tied to that file automatically; use this for precision (one function) or for facts with no Source.

assert_fact.description:
Store a durable fact (subject, predicate, value) in shared memory. A new value for the same
        subject+predicate closes the old one (your own earlier value is superseded; a different agent's value is
        reported in 'contradicts' unless supersede=true). Asserting the same value again is a no-op that returns
        'duplicate_of'. Returns fact_id, superseded[], duplicate_of, contradicts[].

        recallable but are flagged. A first sighting of a file with no old_hash is just a baseline. Returns the
        suspect fact_ids, the decisions built on them, and the docs that describe the changed code. If truncated
        is true, call again with the same arguments (and the returned 'at') to continue.

        contradicted, superseding, from a high-trust source, or suspect are never touched. Dormant facts are hidden
        from recall unless include_dormant=true; restore_fact undoes it.

recall.description:
Search shared memory for facts relevant to a question (semantic + graph expansion), best first. Use this
        before acting, to learn what the team already knows. Each hit has fact_id, text, value, validity window
        and a 'path' showing where it came from. Facts that are used, decided on, or surprising rank a little
        higher; unused old facts rank a little lower but are never hidden. Hits also say whether a fact is
        'suspect' (its code or review date changed: verify before relying on it) and 'protected'. Also returns
        recall_id: pass it to why_recalled to see why these facts came back, in this order.

verify_fact.description:
Record the outcome of re-checking a suspect fact (see facts_to_verify). still_true=true marks it
        verified. still_true=false needs new_value: the new value is asserted, the old one is superseded as of the
        moment the code changed (history stays correct), and decisions that rested on the old value are flagged.

agent_id.description: Your stable agent id, e.g. 'planner' or 'builder-2'. Identifies who is acting.
agent_id.title: Agent Id

commit.description: Optional commit id you verified against.
commit.title: Commit

evidence.description: Optional: where you checked (an absolute file path or URL becomes a Source) or a note.
evidence.title: Evidence

new_value.description: Required when still_true is false: the value it has now.
new_value.title: New Value

step.description: Optional: your own step counter (1, 2, 3...); calls with the same step share one step. If omitted, every call becomes the next step automatically. Never go backwards.
step.title: Step

still_true.description: True if it still holds, false if it changed.
still_true.title: Still True

who_knew.description: Which agents asserted, wrote or READ a fact, and at which step: who knew this, and since when.

agent_id.description: Your stable agent id, e.g. 'planner' or 'builder-2'. Identifies who is acting.
agent_id.title: Agent Id

step.description: Optional: your own step counter (1, 2, 3...); calls with the same step share one step. If omitted, every call becomes the next step automatically. Never go backwards.
step.title: Step

why.description:
Explain WHY a decision was made (or where a fact comes from): the graph paths from a decision_id
            or fact_id to the facts it rests on, who asserted them, their sources, and the steps that wrote them.

agent_id.description: Your stable agent id, e.g. 'planner' or 'builder-2'. Identifies who is acting.
agent_id.title: Agent Id

node_id.description: A decision id or a fact id.
node_id.title: Node Id

step.description: Optional: your own step counter (1, 2, 3...); calls with the same step share one step. If omitted, every call becomes the next step automatically. Never go backwards.
step.title: Step

why_recalled.description:
Explain why a past recall returned the facts it did. The recall_id comes from the recall tool's
            result. Gives the query, each returned fact in rank order with its score, and where it came from.
